"} {"file":"AGENTS.md","output":"# Episodic implementation principles For episode diagrams, follow [docs/EPISODE_DIAGRAMS.md](docs/EPISODE_DIAGRAMS.md). These instructions record the user's design requirements. Read `GOAL.md` and `docs/EPISODE_STRUCTURE.md` and `docs/TIME_AWARE_ESTIMATION.md` before changing execution, estimation or episode behavior. Read the relevant complete implementation paths, not just descriptions or snippets. Current user instructions supersede historical designs and tests. ## Episode ownership - The unit of composition is an intelligence carrying out an iterative problem-solving process. The information library supplies processes that fill a common mother episode template and help construct a child's decision problem, including a small relevant set of alternatives on each turn. Do not substitute tool manuals for process definitions or require a handwritten episode implementation for every problem. Parents supply the job, scope, constraints and requested typed return form; children own their iterative choices. See docs/EPISODE_STRUCTURE.md and docs/TOOL_KNOWLEDGE.md for the design and the current missing construction path. - An episode owns an iterative investigation within its assigned goal and scope. Later decisions use earlier outcomes and can revise the approach. A one-off operation is a tool call, not a new episode. - Execution consists of agentic work and selected tool calls within episodes. Resource instructions, skills and capability discovery are information/tools available there. No additional autonomous workflow layer owns their decisions. - The scientific parent assigns the requested job and its constraints. The launch episode chooses which execution approach to try where that choice is open. Its resource-specific children investigate API/external-service, local compute or HPC execution, receiving the selected job, software instructions, resource instructions and parent-defined handoff form. Preserve explicit parent constraints and caller-owned allocations; infrastructure cannot choose or substitute an approach. This is the user's latest resource-branching direction; the older flat homology launch is not proof it is implemented. - Infrastructure executes and records the selection. It must not substitute, expand or cancel selected work by making an episode-owned decision itself. - The accepted independent-execution design is in docs/EPISODE_STRUCTURE.md. Scientific ownership survives independent execution. Recursive monitors still return parent-defined forms at closure. Waiting is an explicit yield-informed action. Parent yielding does not cancel descendants or reprice closed history. Implement independence in shared method_loop and its durable binding rather than a private background agent loop. Existing blocking children do not prove it. - Episode structure is not a prescribed itinerary. Do not hardcode child order, polling cadence or a number of monitoring children. Do not hide an agent's iterative work in a tool call or a private nested loop outside method_loop. ## Estimates inform decisions - Time/resource estimation and its use in iterative episode decisions are the first implementation priority. Tool execution alone does not establish that episode behavior. - Timing information updates time expectations and earns monitoring credit for having gained timing information. Scientific information earns scientific credit. These remain separate; a job label does not assign information value. - Time-aware estimation supplies duration expectations and their statistical support. It does not select actions, resources, timers, probes or cancellation. - The episode responsible for choosing work needs the relevant information before that choice. A forecast available only after commissioning does not establish informed initial planning. - The parent can choose an inexpensive timing experiment. Do not require such an experiment or fabricate transfer from a small job to a larger one. - Keep scientific credit, monitoring information credit, execution-duration estimates and local yield histories distinct. No master combined score or artificial rescaling/smoothing of raw completed-action credit changes. - Distinguish annotation support from scientific investigation progress. Useful source-grounded qualifications, negative findings and corrections can advance the investigation while lowering the annotation-support hypervolume. That decrease alone is not a scoring defect. Scientific yield should observe investigation progress; report annotation support separately. Do not silently replace the hypervolume formula or reinterpret a saved run's observations. - The configured local yield estimator/controller owns continuation. No hidden stopping rules, turn caps, scientific acceptance gates or approval mechanisms. - Global history shares only typed run statistics. Preserve original expectation snapshots; future learning must not rewrite completed observations or closed child credit. Distinguish queue wait, execution and total turnaround by what was actually measured. Unknown information stays unknown. - Monitoring should expose useful job progress when observable, including relevant log/status information that lets the episode assess loading, throughput or a possible stall. Process liveness alone does not establish productive execution. Preserve measured facts and their provenance; the episode interprets them. See `docs/TIME_AWARE_ESTIMATION.md` for the current interface limits and the distinction from monitoring model-service calls. ## Communication, state and credit - Parents define the information requested from children through forms with declared types and constrained meanings. JSON alone does not constrain prose. Restricted strings are allowed; unrestricted findings/instructions are not. - Recorded facts come from actual records. Child interpretations use the parent's allowed values. Validate references and meaningful field relationships; do not add a separate model call to compose or restate recorded facts. - Actual work, authoritative state, the responsible episode's received information and credit must describe the same contribution. - Record actual outcomes before projecting credit. Distinguish inherited information from new contributions, and completed work from attempted work. Unchanged polling and repeated records do not manufacture progress. - One completed own action supplies one local observation. Internal child work does not become multiple parent observations. Timer firing, statistical refresh and report construction add no synthetic observations. - Preserve valid partial work and return specific structured failures that permit meaningful repair. Termination is not scientific completion. - Archive closed histories to disk and release their live logging/controller state. Keep durable identities and the active information still needed. ## Applying the principles Trace each changed behavior through ownership, selected action, durable state, communication, credit and continuation. Read every affected consumer. A correct local function or a passing test does not prove that this complete path follows the design; tests can encode an implementation mistake. These are implementation responsibilities, not additional runtime gates. Do not introduce a scheduler, reviewer or approval step to enforce them. Report precisely what was inspected, tested and actually run, and what remains unverified. The execution-tool checkout is at `reference/episode_tools`. Its terminology cleanup is separate from this episode build. Its agent roster, procedure, interpreter and stopping behavior are not this workflow's episode structure. The retrievable instruction library is described in `docs/TOOL_KNOWLEDGE.md`. `docs/EPISODE_STRUCTURE.md` distinguishes the accepted target structure from the implemented tree. Categories can aid discovery without mandatory episode levels. Literature and bioinformatics findings can motivate each other; no fixed order or one-way scientific relationship is prescribed. The initial implementation is recorded in [INTEGRATION_PLAN.md](INTEGRATION_PLAN.md), with retained SL1–SL5 items. The later fixed-process/provenance correction is scoped and verified by [FP0–FP7](../../docs/FIXED_PROCESS_BOUNDARIES.md). The library data remains the same 42 separately addressable entries and 208 option/source relationships. The [all-case register](CASE_COVERAGE.md) still accounts for all 142 groups. `ScientificProcessLibrary.freeze(run_directory / "scientific-process-library", source=source_directory)` creates an immutable run snapshot. It pins the source index, entry bodies and per-option provenance rows independently of the research manifest. It retains compact headers in memory; body/source retrieval reads selected files. Reopening uses that snapshot even if the original research directory has changed or disappeared. Reads and reconstruction detect snapshot drift. `process.search`, `process.entry` and `process.sources` are ordinary selected retrieval tools. Their output is instruction provenance with empty scientific record-reference arrays. Source case identifiers never become target observations or credit receipts. The caller explicitly maps a pinned T reference and operation pointer, such as `/capability_operations/0`, to actual callable names and optional argument restrictions. The pointer has meaning only within that exact pinned T body. Suggested repository callables and prose inputs/outputs do not enable operations. Missing callables remain visibly unbound. Several operation-specific restrictions on one callable are alternatives within its actual API constraint. `prepare_scientific_binding(run_directory=..., source_directory=..., mappings=..., child_roles=...)` returns a normal binding descriptor. The caller registers it alongside its actual literature/resource/monitor bindings. Its child roles must include `scientific_process` itself and name actual registered roles. It starts no model or work. Fixed-case callers can explicitly supply `PolicyBindings.execution_planning_roles` to bind prospective duration information to their choosing roles; historical profiles retain their original default.
